title: EPA Greenhouse Gas Data Automation
summary: I developed Python workflows to extract and standardize EPA greenhouse gas reporting data for 2010–2024. API-derived facility tables, FLIGHT classifications and identifier-based reconciliation were combined into reusable CSV outputs, moving from exploratory browser automation toward repeatable facility-level data preparation.
context: Preparation of EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program facility data for downstream environmental and energy research.

image.alt: Conceptual extraction, transformation and delivery diagram for EPA greenhouse gas data
image.caption: Conceptual ETL workflow diagram, not a plot of actual emissions records.

problem: Historical facility emissions records and sector classifications are distributed across EPA tables, reporting-year downloads and the FLIGHT interface. Assembling them consistently requires repeated acquisition, reshaping and reconciliation before the data can support analysis.
contribution: I developed complementary scripts and an exploratory notebook for table discovery, year-specific extraction, facility-level assembly, FLIGHT classification enrichment and standardized exports. I converted much of the exploratory browser work into reusable functions with structured directories, logging and exception handling.

approach.title: Discover tables and assemble facility data
approach.body: EPA_API_Automation.py inspected Envirofacts greenhouse-gas metadata, collected table identifiers and used Selenium to download year-specific CSVs through EPA data services. pandas transformations created facility-by-gas and facility-by-process pivots, joined sector descriptors and merged facility metadata on facility_id, producing Public_Facilities_{year}.csv and intermediate tables.

approach.title: Explore FLIGHT classifications
approach.body: EPA_Flight_Webscrape_11122024.ipynb used Selenium to navigate reporting-year and sector/subsector filters and download Excel exports. BeautifulSoup supported inspection of page elements. Dictionaries keyed by GHGRP facility identifiers linked FLIGHT industry classifications back to the facility tables.

approach.title: Turn exploration into reusable extraction
approach.body: EPA_Flight_Database_Automation.py introduced configurable downloads, reusable functions, structured output directories, file handling, logging and exceptions. It also downloaded summary spreadsheets, identified direct-emitter records and merged selected fields by facility identifier.

approach.title: Reconcile sources and standardize outputs
approach.body: Prefer available FLIGHT sector and subsector values, using EPA API classifications as a fallback where needed. Retain source-related comments, normalize field names and column order, and export facility-level CSVs for subsequent analysis.

approach.title: Make reporting years repeatable
approach.body: Organize extraction, transformation and export around selectable years. The files document complementary stages and workflow evolution rather than proof that three scripts ran sequentially under one production orchestrator.

outcome: The work produced standardized facility-level CSV outputs and documented a path from exploratory web extraction to more reusable automation. It made historical reporting information easier to assemble consistently for environmental research without claiming a measured speedup or a deployed production database.
learning: API tables and web exports can describe the same facility differently. Identifier-based reconciliation and explicit fallback rules make those differences visible and preserve the reason a classification was chosen.
limitations: The supplied scripts establish CSV-based outputs, not a production SQL database load or unified orchestration scheduler.
No measured processing-time savings are reported.
The case study describes methods and verified script behavior; internal implementation files and project-specific data products are not published here.
A conceptual workflow image describes the process and should not be interpreted as emissions data or a measured environmental result.
